test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 26 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which Act provided constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions?
solution:
The correct answer is "**73rd Constitutional Amendment Act 1992**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Due to a number of factors, such as the lack of regular elections, protracted supersession, inadequate representation of weaker groups like women and Scheduled Castes and Tribes, insufficient devolution of power, and a lack of financial resources, it has been observed that Panchayati Raj institutions have not been able to achieve the status and dignity of viable and responsive people's bodies.
 
• As a result, a new amendment to the constitution was added to address gramme panchayat-related issues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Following were the changes made in the constitution:-**

 
 
• Gram Sabha in a village or group of villages.
 
• Panchayats are organised at the village level and other levels.
 
• All positions in Panchayats at the village and intermediate levels, if any, as well as the positions of Panchayat Chairpersons at such levels, shall be filled by direct elections.
 
• Reservation of Panchayat membership and the position of Chairperson in Panchayats at each level for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in proportion to their population.
 
• At least one-third of the seats must be set aside for women.
 
• In the case that a Panchayat is superseded, elections must be held within six months and Panchayats are given a five-year term limit.
 
• Disqualifications for Panchayat membership.
 
• The State Legislature has delegated authority and accountability for developing plans for social justice and economic development as well as carrying out development initiatives to the Panchayats.
 
 
 
• 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act 1992:
 
 
• State Elections Commission is created to conduct elections to PRIs.
 
• Each state must establish a State Finance Commission for a period of five years in order to examine the PRIs' financial standing.
 
• PRIs have a fixed five-year term, and if they are dissolved prematurely, new elections must be held within six months.
 
• The establishment of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system at the zila, block, and village levels,
 
• Elections to PRIs require candidates to be at least 18 years old.
 
• Up to one-third of the seats in panchayats (chairperson and members) are reserved for women.
 
• Reservation of chairman and member positions in panchayats for SC/ST in proportion to their population
 
• At the intermediate and apical tiers, indirect elections for the position of chairman,
 
• Direct elections will be used to fill all positions at all levels (with the exception of two), and
 
• Gram sabhas will be organised.
